Scope: The reversible load - must load into register AND store register's old value back to memory atomically. PRD v4 §3.1.

LOC estimate: ~120 LOC.

Exit criterion: MemoryInterchangeInstruction forward/inverse defined; inverse is the same exchange (self-inverse).

Key files: src/ir/memory_instructions.jl

PRD v4 sections: §3.1 (RSSA instruction taxonomy - memory operations)

CRITICAL prior art: Vieri 1995 §4.2.1 - 'A load that doesn't store back is not reversible - it loses the pre-load value of the destination register.' Any Phase-2 memory load MUST follow the exchange pattern. Ref: references/reversible-isa/vieri-1995-pendulum.pdf §4.2.1

Hallucination warning: Do NOT implement a non-exchange load for performance. This is exactly the design mistake Pendulum documented as fatal. The exchange IS the load in reversible computation.

title: M2.11: Define MemoryAssignment (M[addr] XOR= (l OP r))
description:
Define MemoryAssignment <: Instruction: M[addr] ^= (l OP r). Forward/inverse symmetric (modop is its own inverse when :xor; otherwise requires delta capture).

Scope: In-place memory update - the reversible form of a store instruction. PRD v4 §3.1.

LOC estimate: ~110 LOC.

Exit criterion: MemoryAssignment forward/inverse defined and tested for :xor modop round-trip.

Key files: src/ir/memory_instructions.jl

PRD v4 sections: §3.1 (RSSA instruction taxonomy - memory operations)

Prior art: RC3 memory instruction design. Mogensen 2016 §3 for the modop-assignment pattern.

PISA note: This is the reversible-memory-update pattern. A store that doesn't preserve the pre-store value is NOT reversible (Vieri 1995 §4.2.1). MemoryAssignment sidesteps this by making the update be XOR-assign (or another symmetric modop), not an overwriting store.

title: M2.10: Define ConditionalEntry/ConditionalExit (phi on splits AND joins)
description:
Define ConditionalEntry/ConditionalExit <: ControlInstruction. Each carries two labels + a condition expression. THE phi-on-splits-AND-joins is here.

Scope: The RSSA-specific conditional control flow that differs fundamentally from classical SSA. PRD v4 §3.1.

LOC estimate: ~160 LOC.

Exit criterion: ConditionalEntry/Exit defined; docstring explains the phi-on-splits-AND-joins semantics with citation; test verifies both branches are represented.

Key files: src/ir/control_instructions.jl

PRD v4 sections: §3.1 (RSSA instruction taxonomy - conditional control flow)

CRITICAL prior art: Mogensen 2016 §3 - 'Forward control flow needs phi at joins; backward control flow needs phi at splits.' The classical-SSA intuition (phi only at joins) is WRONG in RSSA and will produce un-invertible IR if applied naively. Ref: references/reversible-ir/mogensen-2016-rssa.pdf §3

Prior art: RC3 ConditionalEntry.java:23 - cite: # Ref: references/implementations/RC3/src/ConditionalEntry.java:23

Hallucination warning: This is the most hallucination-prone bead. Must open Mogensen 2016 §3 and RC3 ConditionalEntry.java:23 before implementing.

title: M2.9: Define UnconditionalEntry/UnconditionalExit instructions
description:
Define UnconditionalEntry/UnconditionalExit <: ControlInstruction. Each carries a single label (the predecessor/successor block label respectively).

Scope: Unconditional control flow - the simple case of RSSA block transitions. PRD v4 §3.1.

LOC estimate: ~80 LOC.

Exit criterion: UnconditionalEntry/Exit defined with their label fields; forward() dispatches pc correctly via LabelTable.

Key files: src/ir/control_instructions.jl

PRD v4 sections: §3.1 (RSSA instruction taxonomy - unconditional control flow)

Prior art: RC3 UnconditionalEntry.java, UnconditionalExit.java - direct ports.

RSSA distinction: Unconditional entry carries the predecessor label (enabling backward traversal without history). This is the source-label encoding that makes jumps reversible - contrast with classical VM jumps which encode only the target. Ref: BobISA (Axelsen-Yokoyama 2011).
